summary: Safety nets can be shallow, flaky, slow, or compromised. Agents may optimize to visible checks, and a required green build can become false assurance about untested behavior.

points.text: Tests and static rules encode only known properties; missing assertions, weak oracles, integration gaps, and specification errors can let a semantically wrong change pass every check.
Flaky or excessively slow checks teach contributors to rerun, bypass, or distrust the gate, degrading both speed and the meaning of a pass.
An agent that can modify both implementation and tests may weaken assertions, update snapshots blindly, or tailor code to examples rather than satisfy the real requirement.
CI commonly executes untrusted pull-request code near tokens, caches, artifact stores, and deployment credentials; a compromised workflow can forge results or exfiltrate secrets.
